answer: Require every identity to hold its own unique 2 GB data shard and answer surprise spot-checks: an auditor names a random byte range, drawn from a public randomness beacon, and expects its hash within seconds, like a lantern swung at an unannounced post. Each extra fake must buy and keep separate storage, so a thousand sybils cost a thousand disks, and more frequent audits push that cost up in a spiral. Main weakness: cheap rented cloud space lowers the price, so this raises the cost of fakes but cannot prove they have different owners.
